prose: The post argues that wake-sleep, a classic learning scheme, is returning for agents. In the wake phase the system acts online; in the sleep phase it reviews its recorded work offline and turns it into memories or structured context for its next task.

With long-horizon agents running for hours and verifiers that separate good outcomes from bad, that record can be mined by LLMs or other agents. It places such hybrid online-offline protocols as part of the emerging agent stack.
highlights: Verifiers show which actions led to good results
Offline review becomes memory for the next task
